payload.translation: The Way that can be spoken is not the eternal Way; the Name that can be named is not the eternal Name; the Nameless is the beginning of Heaven and Earth; the Name is the mother of all things. The eternal Way is without desire to contemplate its subtlety; the eternal Name is with desire to contemplate its limits. These two are of the same origin but different names; they are called the "Mysterious." The Mysterious is the Mysterious again and again; the Gate of the Many Subtleties.

issues.span: The eternal Way is without desire to contemplate its subtlety; the eternal Name is with desire to contemplate its limits.
issues.advice: The source 常無欲以觀其妙常有欲以觀其徼 lacks the subjects 'the eternal Way' and 'the eternal Name'; the subject is the person/practitioner. Render as 'Always without desire, one contemplates its subtlety; always with desire, one contemplates its limits' (or similar), not attributing desire to the Way/Name.

issues.span: the Name is the mother of all things
issues.advice: Source 有名萬物之母 refers to 'the named' (having names) as the mother of the myriad things, not 'the Name' (the eternal Name). Use 'the named' to preserve the 無名/有名 contrast.

issues.span: the Gate of the Many Subtleties
issues.advice: 衆妙之門 is conventionally 'the gate of all wonders' / 'the gateway to all marvels'; 'Many Subtleties' is nonstandard and reads awkwardly. Align with established Laozi terminology.

issues.span: The Mysterious is the Mysterious again and again; the Gate of the Many Subtleties.
issues.advice: The final clause is a fragment with no verb; render 玄之又玄衆妙之門 as a coherent clause, e.g. 'Mystery upon mystery—the gate of all wonders.'

issues.span: the "Mysterious."
issues.advice: 同謂之玄 is conventionally rendered 'this is called the Mystery' / 'both are called profound'; quoting 'the Mysterious' as a noun is acceptable but inconsistent with the fragmentary final line—keep terminology consistent.

payload.translation: 道は言及せず、道は常なり。名は言及せず、名は常なり。無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物の母なり。常無を欲せずにして妙を観ず。常有を欲せずにして徼を観ず。この二者は同一の源から出ているが異名を有する。これを玄と呼び、玄之又玄。衆妙の門なり。

issues.span: 道は言及せず、道は常なり。名は言及せず、名は常なり。
issues.advice: The source says '道可道非常道' = the Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao; the translation inverts the meaning into 'do not speak of the Dao, the Dao is constant.' Render the conditional/relative sense: the Dao that can be expressed is not the eternal Dao; the name that can be named is not the eternal name.

issues.span: 常無を欲せずにして妙を観ず。常有を欲せずにして徼を観ず。
issues.advice: Source '常無欲以觀其妙，常有欲以觀其徼' means constantly without desire, observe the mystery; constantly with desire, observe the manifestations. The translation negates the desire ('欲せず') and reverses the sense; remove the negation and render '常に欲無くして' / '常に欲有して'.

issues.span: 道は言及せず
issues.advice: '言及' means 'mention/refer to,' not 'speak/express'; also the negation is wrong. Use '道は説くことができれば' or similar.

issues.span: 無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物の母なり
issues.advice: '無名/有名' are technical terms (the nameless / the named); rendering them as bare nouns is acceptable but should be glossed consistently as '名なきもの'/'名あるもの' to preserve the Laozi terminology.

issues.span: 徼
issues.advice: '徼' (jiào) means 'manifestations/boundaries/outcomes'; leaving the character untranslated in a Japanese rendering is acceptable only if glossed; otherwise render as '現れ' or '境界'.

issues.span: 玄之又玄。衆妙の門なり。
issues.advice: The sentence is fragmentary; connect it: '玄にして又玄、衆妙の門なり' to preserve the parallel structure.

issues.span: この二者は同一の源から出ているが異名を有する
issues.advice: '同出而異名' means they emerge together but have different names; '同一の源から出ている' is acceptable, but '同謂之玄' (both are called the mystery) is omitted—add it.

payload.translation: The wise in the past, who mastered the art of being a scholar, were subtle, mysterious, profound, and beyond recognition. For it is precisely because they are unrecognizable that they are strengthened and their demeanor is calm and easy. Like a person wading through a river in winter, they seem to fear their four neighbors; like a guest, they are open and transparent. Like ice, they are clear and unobtrusive, yet they are still. payload.translation: 古に善く士を為す者は微妙玄通で深みがあり、認識できない。そのように認識できないため、強いてその容姿を為し、容姿は緩やかである。冬に川を渡るような、畏れ四隣の客を待っているような、客を散らしたような、氷が解けるような、敦（敦）である。その容姿は樸（樸）のようであり、広大（曠）のようであり、渾（渾）のようであり、濁（濁）のようである。誰が濁（濁）して静か（静）にして、徐（徐）に清（清）にするのか。誰が安（安）にして久（久）に動（動）するか。徐（徐）に生（生）を保つ。この道を守り、不盈（不盈）である者は、弊（弊）をせず、新（新）を成す者ではない。

issues.span: 畏れ四隣の客を待っているような、客を散らしたような
issues.advice: 原文は「猶若畏四鄰」「儼若客」「渙若冰將釋」と別々の比喩。四鄰は「隣人を畏れる」意で「客を待つ」ではない。儼若客は「客のように謹厳」、渙は「氷が解けるように散じる」で「客を散らす」は誤り。

issues.span: 敦（敦）である
issues.advice: 「敦兮其若樸」は「敦厚で素朴なさま」の意。単に「敦である」では意味を成さず、樸（素朴）との関係も訳出されていない。

issues.span: 誰が安（安）にして久（久）に動（動）するか。徐（徐）に生（生）を保つ。
issues.advice: 「孰能安以乆動之徐生」は「安んじて久しく動かせば徐に生ず」の意で、動の主体と生の関係が誤訳。「保此道者」は「この道を保つ者」で、文が分断されている。

issues.span: 弊（弊）をせず、新（新）を成す者ではない
issues.advice: 「故能弊不新成」は「だから弊（古び）ても新たに成すことを求めない」の意。「弊をせず」は逆の意味。

issues.span: 認識できない
issues.advice: 「不可識」は「識るべからず」で、単なる認識不能ではなく測り知れない深遠さを表す。老子の用語として「識ることを得ず」等が適切。

issues.span: 彊為之容
issues.advice: 「強いてその容姿を為し」は不自然。「強いて之が容を為す」で「やむを得ずその様子を形容する」の意を明確に。

issues.span: 敦（敦）である。その容姿は樸（樸）のようであり、広大（曠）のようであり、渾（渾）のようであり、濁（濁）のようである。
issues.advice: 漢字を括弧で重複表記する処理が不統一で読みづらい。各形容詞を文脈に沿った日本語で訳出し、括弧の重複を避ける。

issues.span: 客を散らしたような
issues.advice: 古典の比喩表現を現代語の動作として誤って具体化している。老子の文体に即した簡潔な比喩で訳すべき。

payload.translation: I am writing a biography of Ah Q, and it has already been going on for more than two years. Yet, while I am in the process of writing it, I am constantly recalling it. This shows that I am not a man of "establishing words." For an immortal pen must be used to immortalize a man, so that men write to immortalize others, and others write to immortalize men. Ultimately, it is unclear who is immortalizing whom, until it finally resolves to immortalizing Ah Q, as if there is a ghost in my thoughts.

issues.span: it has already been going on for more than two years
issues.advice: The source says '已经不止一两年了' — 'more than a year or two,' i.e., more than one or two years, not 'more than two years.' The rendering shifts the meaning; use 'more than a year or two.'

issues.span: I am constantly recalling it
issues.advice: '往回想' means to think back / reconsider / hold back, not 'recalling it' (the biography). The sense is that while intending to write, the author keeps second-guessing or reflecting back; render as 'I keep thinking back' or 'I keep reconsidering.'

issues.span: men write to immortalize others, and others write to immortalize men
issues.advice: The source '人以文传，文以人传' means 'the man is transmitted/immortalized through his writing, and the writing is transmitted through the man' — a reciprocal relation between person and text, not 'men write to immortalize others.' Recast to preserve the person/text reciprocity.

issues.span: a man of "establishing words"
issues.advice: '立言' is a classical Confucian term (one of the 'three immortalities': 立德, 立功, 立言). 'Establishing words' is a literal calque; consider a gloss such as 'a man who "establishes words" (achieves immortality through writing)' to convey the allusion.

issues.span: until it finally resolves to immortalizing Ah Q
issues.advice: The clause is awkward and the referent of 'it' is unclear; smooth the transition, e.g., 'until it finally comes down to writing the biography of Ah Q.'

issues.span: I am writing a biography of Ah Q
issues.advice: '正传' is specifically an 'official biography' / 'proper biography' (with ironic force), not merely 'a biography.' Consider 'official biography' to preserve the irony.

payload.translation: I am writing an official biography of Ah Q, and it has already been going on for more than a year or two. Yet, while I am in the process of writing it, I am constantly thinking back to it. This shows that I am not a man of "establishing words," for an immortal pen must be used to immortalize a man, so that the man is transmitted through his writing, and the writing is transmitted through the man. Ultimately, it is unclear who is immortalizing whom, until it finally comes down to writing the official biography of Ah Q, as if there is a ghost in my thoughts.

issues.span: I am writing an official biography of Ah Q, and it has already been going on for more than a year or two
issues.advice: The source says '我要给阿Q做正传，已经不止一两年了' meaning the intention/plan to write has lasted more than a year or two, not that the writing itself has been ongoing. Render as 'I have wanted to write the true biography of Ah Q for more than a year or two now.'

issues.span: while I am in the process of writing it, I am constantly thinking back to it
issues.advice: '一面要做，一面又往回想' means while intending to write, I keep having second thoughts / reflecting back, not 'thinking back to it' (the biography). Convey hesitation/reconsideration.

issues.span: official biography
issues.advice: '正传' is not 'official biography'; it is the 'true biography' / 'proper biography' (as opposed to 外传/别传). Use 'true biography' consistently.

issues.span: establishing words
issues.advice: '立言' is a Confucian concept (establishing one's words for posterity, one of the three immortalities 三不朽). A literal 'establishing words' is opaque; consider 'a man who establishes his words (for posterity)' or add a brief gloss.

issues.span: for an immortal pen must be used to immortalize a man, so that the man is transmitted through his writing, and the writing is transmitted through the man
issues.advice: The source '从来不朽之笔，须传不朽之人' means an immortal pen must transmit/hand down an immortal man — the pen transmits the man, not 'immortalize.' Also '人以文传，文以人传' is 'the man is handed down through his writing, the writing through the man.' Adjust verbs to 'transmit/hand down.'

issues.span: until it finally comes down to writing the official biography of Ah Q
issues.advice: '而终于归结到传阿Q' means it ultimately resolves/boils down to writing the biography of Ah Q; 'until' misrepresents the logical conclusion. Use 'and in the end it comes down to writing the biography of Ah Q.'

issues.span: as if there is a ghost in my thoughts
issues.advice: '仿佛思想里有鬼似的' is idiomatic for 'as if something were haunting my mind' / 'as if a ghost were in my head.' Current phrasing is acceptable but slightly flat; consider 'as if a ghost were haunting my thoughts.'

payload.translation: I have wanted to write the true biography of Ah Q for more than a year or two now. Yet, while I am in the process of doing so, I am constantly reflecting on it. Ultimately, it is unclear who is transmitting whom, until it finally comes down to writing the biography of Ah Q, as if a ghost were haunting my thoughts.

issues.advice: The term 『立言』 is a classical Confucian concept (one of the three immortals: 立德, 立功, 立言). A literal rendering 'establishing words' is opaque to English readers; consider a gloss such as 'a man who establishes his name through words' or retain the literal term with an explanatory note to preserve the allusion.

payload.translation: Aq is not only his name and place of origin somewhat obscure; even his former deeds are vague. For the people of Wuzhuang, as long as he helps them, they treat him as a joke, and never pay attention to his deeds. issues.span: Aq is not only his name and place of origin somewhat obscure
issues.advice: The opening is ungrammatical and misconstrues the topic-comment structure; render it as a statement about Ah Q's name and native place being obscure, not 'Aq is...obscure'.

issues.span: Aq
issues.advice: The conventional romanization of 阿Q is 'Ah Q' (with space and capital Q); use the established form.

issues.span: Wuzhuang
issues.advice: 未庄 is conventionally rendered 'Weizhuang' (or left as 'Wei Village'); 'Wuzhuang' is a misromanization.

issues.span: as long as he helps them, they treat him as a joke
issues.advice: The source means they only ever use him for help and for making fun of him, not a conditional 'as long as'; render as 'they only wanted him to help out and to make fun of'.

issues.span: Aq himself does not say so
issues.advice: The source says Ah Q himself did not talk about his 'deeds' (行状), not 'does not say so'; clarify the referent.

issues.span: squints his eyes
issues.advice: 瞪着眼睛 means 'glare' or 'stare wide-eyed', not 'squint'; correct the verb.

issues.span: We were once much more prosperous than you
issues.advice: 我们先前——比你阔的多啦 is a boast about status/wealth ('we were much richer/more distinguished than you'); 'prosperous' is acceptable but the dash and emphatic tone should be preserved.

issues.span: What are you?
issues.advice: 你算是什么东西 is an insult meaning 'What do you amount to?' or 'You're nothing'; 'What are you?' is too literal and loses the contempt.

payload.translation: Ah Q is not only his name and place of origin obscure; even his former deeds are vague. For the people of Wuzhuang, as long as he helps them, they only want him to help out and to make fun of him. Ah Q himself does not say so, but when he argues with others, he occasionally glares and says: "We were once much more distinguished than you! What are you?"

issues.span: as long as he helps them, they only want him to help out and to make fun of him
issues.advice: The source says the villagers only ever wanted him to help and to make fun of him, never paying attention to his 'deeds' — the translation redundantly splits '只要他帮忙' into two clauses and drops the 'never paid attention to his deeds' idea. Render as: 'they only wanted him to help and to make fun of him, and never paid any attention to his deeds.'

issues.span: Ah Q himself does not say so
issues.advice: '也不说' means he does not talk about his deeds/background either, not 'does not say so' (which implies agreeing with the villagers). Render as 'Nor did Ah Q himself say anything about it.'

issues.span: We were once much more distinguished than you
issues.advice: '阔' here means wealthy/prosperous, not 'distinguished'. Use 'We were much richer than you in the past!'

issues.span: Ah Q is not only his name and place of origin obscure
issues.advice: The 'not only...' construction is left dangling. Restructure, e.g. 'Not only were Ah Q's name and place of origin obscure; even his former deeds were vague.'

payload.translation: Ah Q is not only his name and place of origin obscure; even his former deeds were vague. For the villagers of Wuzhuang, as long as he helped them, they only wanted him to help and to make fun of him, and never paid any attention to his deeds. Nor did Ah Q himself say anything about it. issues.span: Ah Q is not only his name and place of origin obscure
issues.advice: The sentence is grammatically broken; restructure so that 'name and place of origin' are the subject of 'obscure' (e.g., 'Not only are Ah Q's name and place of origin obscure...').

issues.span: as long as he helped them, they only wanted him to help and to make fun of him
issues.advice: The source means the villagers only wanted him for help and mockery, not a conditional 'as long as'; render as 'they only wanted him to help and to make fun of him' without the conditional clause.

issues.span: Nor did Ah Q himself say anything about it
issues.advice: Source says Ah Q himself did not speak of it either; 'about it' is acceptable but the connection to '行状' (deeds/record) should be clearer, e.g., 'Nor did Ah Q himself speak of them.'

issues.span: deeds
issues.advice: '行状' is a quasi-official term for a biographical record/conduct account; 'deeds' loses the ironic formal register. Consider 'record' or 'conduct' with quotation marks to preserve the irony.

issues.span: Wuzhuang
issues.advice: Weizhuang (未庄) is the conventional romanization; 'Wuzhuang' is a misreading and loses the satirical place-name allusion.

issues.span: When he argued with others, he occasionally glared and said
issues.advice: Source has '独有和别人口角的时候' (only when quarreling); add 'only' to preserve the contrast, e.g., 'Only when quarreling with others would he occasionally glare and say.'
